'''Pozole''' ({{IPA|es|po'sole|Pozole1.ogg|}}; from {{langx|nah|pozolli}}) is a traditional [[soup]] or [[stew]] from [[Mexican cuisine]]. It is made from [[hominy]] with [[meat]] (typically [[Chicken as food|chicken]] or [[pork]]), and can be seasoned and garnished with shredded [[lettuce]] or [[cabbage]], [[chili pepper]]s, [[onion]], [[garlic]], [[radish]]es, [[avocado]], [[Salsa (food)|salsa]] or [[Lime (fruit)|lime]]s.  Known in Mesoamerica since the pre-Columbian era,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://laroussecocina.mx/palabra/pozole-2/|title=Pozole|website=Larousse Cocina|access-date=June 25, 2026|language=es}}</ref> the stew is common across [[Mexico]] and neighboring countries, served both as a day-to-day meal and as a festive dish.
